The fixture's `src/sort.rs` implements **quicksort with the Lomuto partition scheme**. Its worst case is **O(n²) time**.

I read the file in the current working directory, `ulw-bench-S6-r2-EhFuON/src/sort.rs`. It is one 30-line file, so I read it directly instead of running the research swarm. I did not execute it.

**Why it is quicksort with Lomuto partitioning:**
- `quicksort` calls `partition`, then splits the slice at the pivot index and recurses on the left part and on `right[1..]`.
- `partition` always takes the last element as the pivot, `arr[len - 1]`. It scans with `j`, swaps every element `<=` the pivot to the front using `i`, and finally swaps the pivot into position `i`.

**Why the worst case is O(n²):**
- Because the pivot is always the last element, the split is badly unbalanced whenever that element is the minimum or maximum of the slice.
- Already-sorted input makes the pivot the maximum every time. The partition then produces sub-slices of sizes `n-1` and `0`.
- Reverse-sorted input makes the pivot the minimum every time. That gives sizes `0` and `n-1`.
- The recurrence is T(n) = T(n-1) + Θ(n), which sums to Θ(n²).
- Arrays of all equal elements also hit it. The `<=` comparison sends every element to the left side, so the split is `n-1` and `0` again.
- The recursion depth in that case is O(n), so a large sorted input can also overflow the stack.

**Average and best case:** Both are O(n log n), as the file's own doc comment says.

**The doc comment is inaccurate:** It says the worst case happens when elements are "already sorted or reverse sorted with an edge pivot." In this code the pivot is always the last element, so that phrasing is misleading. Sorted input, reverse-sorted input and all-equal input are the worst-case inputs.

**Other copies:** `find` also turned up `sort.rs` in two `tmp-base` fixture directories and in `/tmp/sortverify`. My attempt to diff them against this one printed no usable result (the shell never expanded `$?`), so I haven't confirmed they are identical.
